prompt_fields.subject: A huge hunched spider seen from a steep overhead three-quarter angle: bulbous dark abdomen, eight legs radiating low and wide around the body, small cluster of glowing red eyes on a forward-lowered head. Body held low and broad rather than tall.
prompt_fields.contrast: First spiderkin/spider identity in the catalog, so no in-family collision; the silhouette (low broad radial 8-leg spread, no other current token shares that shape) and the glowing red eye-cluster (the one bright value accent on an otherwise dark body) are the identity anchors.
prompt_fields.composition: One compact complete creature on a single circular tabletop disc, steep overhead three-quarter camera; visible clear neutral base ring on every side. Keep all anatomy and equipment well inside the inner four-fifths of disc radius. Base brightness must visually match reference neutral disc, with no illumination spill or ground effects. Base-plate discipline, calibrated: this batch (monster-boss-e, same style reference) has now been measured on three fresh (non-edit) generations -- an initial "8 units darker" instruction produced base_drift -9.23, -12.21 and -15.18 (all overshooting the +-8 tolerance on the dark side), while a follow-up "4 units darker" instruction on the same identity landed at -5.11, cleanly inside tolerance. Render the neutral disc -- including the whole outer-sixth ring band -- only about 4 RGB luminance units darker than the style reference's disc appears at first read: a small, conservative undershoot, not a full shade darker. Do not darken the creature itself to compensate -- only the disc plate takes this small intentional downward bias. Add no warm cast, glow, bounce-light, gradient or vignette to the disc anywhere, including directly under or behind dark-bodied creatures.
prompt_fields.palette: Near-black charcoal carapace with a faint deep-violet sheen, small cluster of glowing ember-red eyes, dull grey-brown leg tips; dry neutral charcoal disc with restrained copper-grey bevel -- keep the dark body from merging into the disc by preserving a lighter facing plane on the forward legs and head.
